Revenue is around $16-17 billion. Listed on the NYSE under CTVA, and in 2025 it announced plans to separate its seed and crop protection businesses. Strong brand with farmers, almost no consumer awareness.

about: WayCool is a Chennai-based Indian food and agri-tech company that sources fruits, vegetables, dairy and staples from farmers and supplies them to retailers, restaurants and institutional buyers and runs its own food processing and branded product lines. It operates cold chains and a platform for B2B buyers across South India. It is a B2B food supply brand with growing regional recognition.

Nigeria's largest industrial conglomerate, owned by Aliko Dangote, with businesses in cement (Dangote Cement, listed in Lagos), sugar refining, salt, flour, fertiliser, packaging and a large oil refinery and petrochemical complex at Lekki. It supplies basic consumer and construction goods across Nigeria and into other African countries, and earns money from product sales and exports. Headquartered in Lagos with tens of thousands of staff. The Dangote name is among the most visible commercial brands in Africa and the group sponsors football, boxing and charity events.

US chemical manufacturer producing nitrogen-based products including ammonia, nitric acid, ammonium nitrate and urea for agricultural, industrial and mining customers, with plants in Arkansas, Alabama, Oklahoma and Texas. Based in Oklahoma City and listed on the NYSE (LXU), it has revenue near 500 million dollars. Customers are farmers through distributors, mining companies and industrial buyers. B2B with limited consumer awareness.

Zhejiang Fenglong Electric is a manufacturer and distributor based in Shaoxing, Zhejiang, China, tagged by Crunchbase under agriculture and automotive. The name points to electric products, such as motors or electrical components for farm machinery and vehicles, but the data given does not confirm its exact products, customers, size or ownership. It is a B2B industrial supplier without consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: One of Japan's big five trading houses (sogo shosha), active in grain and food supply, power generation and infrastructure, metals, chemicals, aerospace and retail partnerships, with grain handling through Columbia Grain in the US. It profits from trading margins, project investments and equity earnings in dozens of countries. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (8002) and partly held by Berkshire Hathaway. Large corporate with tens of thousands of staff; strong B2B name, modest consumer visibility.

US indoor vertical farming company that grew leafy greens and herbs on towers in controlled warehouses, supplying retailers such as Walmart and restaurants, and had a major robotics-heavy farm in Compton, California. It was backed by SoftBank and investors linked to Jeff Bezos and Bezos Expeditions, but economics were hard and it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2025. Modest consumer brand profile and weak financial position.

about: Global seed company that develops and sells hybrid seeds for corn, sorghum, sunflower, canola and rice, with research stations in Asia, Africa, Latin America, Australia and Europe. Customers are farmers and agribusiness distributors in over 50 countries, and income comes from seed sales. It is a subsidiary of the Indian agrochemical group UPL, with outside investors such as Brookfield and Alpha Wave taking stakes in 2024. Brand recognition is strong among farmers and seed dealers but zero among consumers.

about: German agricultural and construction trading group, based in Munich, trading grain, fertiliser and farm machinery, supplying building materials through BayWa Baustoffe, and running the renewable energy developer BayWa r.e. It serves farmers, builders and utilities in Germany, Austria and abroad, and employs about 20,000 people. Owned by a cooperative, it faced a financial crisis in 2023 and 2024 and underwent a restructuring with lenders. Well known to German farmers and tradespeople.

Ukraine's largest poultry and agribusiness company, producing chicken under the Nasha Ryaba and Lehko brands, plus vegetable oils, grain and meat processed products sold in Ukraine, the EU, the Middle East and Asia. It also runs big farm and feed operations and has a large employee base. Controlled by Yuriy Kosyuk, it is listed in London through global depositary receipts, with operations hit by the war but still running. Prominent national consumer food brand.

US company based in Louisville, Colorado, tagged under agriculture, commercial and digital asset management, listed under the name BNB Standard. about: US biotech that developed cell-free RNA production, including double-stranded RNA sprays such as Calantha used to protect crops from pests like the Colorado potato beetle, plus RNA vaccines and therapeutics. Customers are farmers and agricultural distributors, and it became public through a SPAC in 2022 but ran into funding trouble and delisted in 2023. Based in Medford, Massachusetts. Specialist agtech name with very low consumer awareness.

about: US indoor vertical farming company that grows produce, including lettuce, tomatoes and herbs, in controlled automated farms, and sells to grocery chains such as Kroger and to foodservice customers. It runs farms in Ohio and other US states and acquired Infinite Acres. Customers are grocers and restaurants, with revenue from produce sales. Private, backed by firms including Spark Capital, with growing consumer shelf presence but a niche brand.

about: Canadian renewable energy company based in Toronto that builds and operates anaerobic digestion plants converting food waste, grease and other organic waste into biogas and electricity, with a flagship plant in London, Ontario. Customers are food processors, waste haulers and utilities, with income from waste tipping fees, energy sales and fertiliser by-products. Privately held. Local sustainability profile and little general public awareness.

about: Large US public research university in Urbana and Champaign, Illinois, with about 56,000 students and a major engineering, computing and agriculture reputation, plus a research park and the NCSA supercomputing centre. Funding comes from state appropriations, tuition, grants and philanthropy. Its Fighting Illini teams compete in the Big Ten and attract a large alumni and fan base. Recognised as a flagship university across the US, with real sports-marketing relevance through athletics.

Halter is a New Zealand agtech company that makes a solar-powered smart collar for cattle, which lets farmers move, steer and monitor herds from a phone app using sound and vibration cues instead of fences. Customers are dairy and beef farmers in New Zealand, Australia and the US, who pay hardware and subscription fees. Founded in 2016 by Craig Piggott and based in Auckland, it is venture-backed (Bond, Blackbird and others) and has been valued at around 1 billion dollars. Well known among farmers, with modest general awareness.

Ninjacart is an Indian business-to-business fresh produce supply chain platform which buys fruit and vegetables directly from farmers and delivers them to retailers, restaurants and kirana stores in cities such as Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai and Mumbai. It earns revenue from the margin on produce and logistics, and uses data and technology to cut waste. Founded in 2015 in Bengaluru, backed by Walmart, Tiger Global and Flipkart. A B2B brand with little consumer awareness, though recognised in the Indian agritech sector.

Oishii is a US vertical farming company that grows premium strawberries, including its Omakase Berry, in indoor vertical farms in New Jersey using pollination by bees in controlled environments. Customers are consumers and high-end retailers like Whole Foods, restaurants and grocery stores, sold under the Oishii brand. Founded in 2016 in Japan and later based in New Jersey, it is backed by Wicklow and others. A niche premium consumer food brand with limited broad awareness.

West Fraser Timber is a Canadian forest products company and one of the world's largest lumber producers, making lumber, plywood, oriented strand board (OSB), medium-density fibreboard and pulp, with mills in western Canada, the US South and Europe (after buying Norbord in 2021). Customers are builders and wholesale distributors. Revenue is in the billions of dollars and it has more than 10,000 staff. Listed on the TSX and NYSE (WFG), founded in 1955 in British Columbia. A B2B commodity producer with little consumer awareness.

BlackSoil is an Indian non-bank lender and advisory firm based in Mumbai, offering structured credit and venture debt to growing businesses, with a background in agriculture and rural finance, and supporting investors. It reports roughly 310 million dollars of funding. Revenue comes from interest and fees. Privately held with little consumer awareness, known mainly to small and mid-size Indian businesses and financial investors. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: JAPFA Group is an Indonesian-based agribusiness group, one of Southeast Asia's large integrated poultry and food companies, producing animal feed, day-old chicks, broilers, dairy products (Greenfields) and consumer food brands such as Real Good and So Good, along with aquaculture and beef feedlots. Customers are farmers, retailers and mass consumers, with operations in Indonesia, Vietnam, Myanmar and India. The Indonesian arm is listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (JPFA). Some consumer brands are well known in Indonesia.

Vital Farms is a US food company selling pasture-raised eggs and butter under the Vital Farms brand, sourced from a network of several hundred small family farms and certified humane, with products in thousands of stores including Whole Foods, Kroger and Target. Customers are health-conscious US consumers, and revenue is around 500 to 600 million dollars. Founded in 2007 and based in Austin, Texas, and listed on Nasdaq (VITL) since 2020. A growing consumer food brand with strong social media marketing and brand visibility among US households.

Chinese online agricultural products marketplace, Meicai, based in Beijing, that supplies fresh vegetables, meat and other produce to restaurants, small grocers and canteens, using a platform that connects farm suppliers with buyers and delivers from its own warehouses. Founded in 2014 by Liu Chuanjun, with backing from Tiger Global, Hillhouse, Tencent and others. It has cut operations in recent years amid losses. B2B brand little known to consumers.

Indian financing arm of CNH Industrial, the maker of Case IH and New Holland tractors and construction equipment, providing retail loans to farmers and contractors and wholesale financing to dealers. CNH Industrial is an Italian-American group listed on the NYSE, so the record shows Turin as location, but the operations sit in India. Revenue is from interest and fees on equipment loans. Captive finance brand with low independent profile, though tied to well-known farm machinery brands.

about: Trimble is a US technology company, based in Westminster, Colorado, that sells positioning, GPS, software and sensor systems. Its products serve construction (Tekla, SketchUp, machine control), geospatial surveying, agriculture and transportation fleets, sold to contractors, engineers, farmers and logistics firms through hardware plus subscription software. Founded in 1978 and listed on Nasdaq (TRMB), it employs around 12,000 people and earns about 3.5 billion dollars of annual revenue. In 2024 it moved its agriculture business into a joint venture with AGCO. B2B brand with strong industry recognition but low consumer awareness.

Apeel Sciences is a Goleta, California food technology company that makes Apeel, a plant-derived edible coating applied to fresh fruit and vegetables, such as avocados, citrus and cucumbers, to slow moisture loss and spoilage and extend shelf life. Customers are growers, packers, distributors and retailers including Costco, Kroger and Aldi, paying for coated produce or application services. Founded in 2012, it has raised over 700 million dollars from backers including Viking Global, Temasek, Bill Gates and Oprah Winfrey, and was valued around 2 billion dollars. B2B ingredient, visible to consumers only through a produce label.

AppHarvest was a Kentucky agritech company, based in Morehead, that built large high-tech greenhouses to grow tomatoes, cucumbers and leafy greens using recycled rainwater, selling to US grocers and food distributors under its own brand. Founded in 2018 by Jonathan Webb, it listed on Nasdaq (APPH) through a SPAC merger in February 2021 and attracted backing from celebrities and Martha Stewart. Chronic losses and operating problems led to a Chapter 11 filing in July 2023. Its consumer brand was limited to US grocery produce shelves and had modest awareness.

Ameropa is a privately owned Swiss agricultural trading group, headquartered in Binningen near Basel, founded in 1948. It trades and distributes fertilizers, grain and other agri commodities, and also owns fertilizer production and storage assets and agribusiness operations in Romania, Ukraine and other markets. Customers are farmers, cooperatives, processors and importers worldwide, and its revenue has run to many billions of dollars a year. The group is held by private owners and funded by banks. It is an agricultural supply chain business with low consumer brand awareness but strong standing among commodity traders.

about: K+S is a German mining and salt company based in Kassel, listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (SDF) and part of the MDAX. It produces potash and magnesium fertilizers sold to farmers, industrial salts for chemical and food uses, de-icing salt, and consumer products such as pet litter and table salt under brands like Esco. Operations include mines in Germany and the Bethune potash mine in Saskatchewan, Canada, with annual revenue of roughly 3 to 4 billion euros and about 11,000 employees. Founded in 1889 as Kali und Salz. Mostly B2B, with some consumer salt products, and recognised in Germany.

CPM Holdings is a Blaine, Minnesota industrial engineering group that supplies machinery and consumables for animal feed, pet food, biomass and oilseed processing. Its brands include California Pellet Mill, CPM Roskamp Champion, Beta Raven and Extru-Tech, selling pellet mills, extruders, flaking mills and process automation to feed manufacturers, grain processors and food companies in more than 100 countries. With roots going back to the 1800s, it has several thousand employees and annual revenue approaching 1 billion dollars. Privately held and long owned by private equity. B2B equipment maker, known in agriculture but not to consumers.

about: Kernel Holding is a Ukrainian agribusiness group headquartered in Kyiv, listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (KER) and run by Andriy Verevskyi. It is the largest sunflower oil producer and a major exporter of Ukrainian grain, oilseeds and bottled oil, farming several hundred thousand hectares and operating oilseed crushing plants, grain silos and a Black Sea port terminal. Customers are food processors, traders and retailers across Europe, Asia and the Middle East. The war in Ukraine has disrupted operations and export routes. Mainly B2B, with bottled oil sold under consumer brands in Ukraine.

AgDevCo is a London-based specialist investor in agriculture and agribusiness in Sub-Saharan Africa, providing patient capital to farms, processors and food supply chains, such as horticulture, dairy, grains, aquaculture and cold storage. Founded in 2009 with funding from the UK government and other development backers, including the Gates Foundation, it makes equity and debt investments and works with local entrepreneurs, aiming for both financial return and jobs and food security. It holds investments in countries including Zambia, Ghana, Nigeria and Tanzania. B2B development finance firm, little consumer visibility.

about: Yellow Cake plc is a London-based Jersey-incorporated investment company listed on the AIM market of the London Stock Exchange (YCA), whose purpose is to hold physical uranium (U3O8) as a way for investors to gain exposure to the uranium price. It buys uranium from Kazatomprom under a supply agreement and stores it at conversion facilities, with net assets in the hundreds of millions of pounds and a small management team at Yellow Cake's adviser Tavira. Customers are shareholders, and it does not mine. B2B finance business with little consumer awareness.

AeroFarms is an American vertical farming company, founded in 2004 and best known for growing leafy greens indoors in stacked trays using aeroponic misting rather than soil or sunlight, sold under the Dream Greens brand in US grocery stores. It operated large indoor farms in New Jersey and Virginia and had a research partnership in Abu Dhabi, backed by investors including Ingka and Goldman Sachs. After heavy losses it filed for Chapter 11 in June 2023 and later emerged from bankruptcy with a leaner business, with funding of about 314 million dollars. Moderate US grocery brand visibility.

Goodleaf Farms is a Canadian vertical farming company based in Guelph, Ontario, which grows leafy greens, herbs and microgreens indoors in stacked trays under LED lighting using hydroponics, with no pesticides. It sells packaged salad greens and herbs to supermarkets such as Loblaw, Sobeys and Metro across Canada, under its own Goodleaf brand and retailer labels, and operates farms in Guelph, Montreal and other sites. Founded in 2014, it has raised about 285 million dollars, including a major round in 2025. Consumer-facing grocery brand with regional visibility in Canada.
